author: BBC News
description:
The US has carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, US officials have told CBS, the BBC's US partner.
 
The officials described the strikes as limited and defensive, and said they were in response to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) firing on a US aircraft.
 
Iranian state news agency Irna reported explosions on Qeshm on Monday. The IRGC did not comment but said its forces had shot down two US MQM-170 drones south of the island and a US MQ-9 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz.
 
The US military has not commented on the strikes, which came as mediators stepped up their efforts to prevent a return to all-out war after the US midterm elections on Tuesday.

Could the UK's push to become an AI superpower put its 2050 net zero target at risk?

The UK government wants to rapidly expand the number of AI data centres being built across the country, but a BBC File on 4 Investigates report has found this rapid growth could severely affect the government's own net zero climate goals. 

Plans for some of the biggest sites include proposals for on-site gas power stations to feed the energy-hungry data centres. This is because developers cannot immediately connect to the national grid - with potential waits of up to 10 years.

BBC calculations suggest that if four of these gas-fuelled mega data centres ran at full capacity all year, they could produce more carbon emissions than Manchester, Liverpool and Southampton combined.

description:
Millions of Americans are casting their votes for House, Senate and gubernatorial candidates in the 2026 midterm elections. And while President Donald Trump is not on the ballot, this is a pivotal moment for his presidency, which could shape his final two years in the White House, and his political legacy. 

Democrats are hoping to capitalise on concerns about high costs of living, exacerbated by President Trump's tariffs and the war with Iran. Opinion polling suggests the Democrats could take control of both houses of Congress, but many key races are within the margin of error. Close Senate races are forecast in several previously reliable Republican states, including Texas, Alaska, Iowa, Kansas and Ohio. 

In this video, we visit some of these battleground states, and find out how issues like rising fuel costs, immigration and affordable healthcare are affecting voters.

description:
In a compelling new interview, veteran investigative reporter John North recounts his unforgettable experience of witnessing the failed execution attempt of death row inmate Christa Pike. 
 
Pike was sentenced to death in Tennessee after the brutal 1995 murder of student Colleen Slemmer. For years, her case has remained one of the state's most notorious criminal stories. 

As an official media witness, John North was granted access to events unfolding inside the prison during the state's attempt to carry out Pike's execution – which did not go to plan. 
 
The Tennessee Department of Correction has not explained why the execution did not go as planned, though it has defended the method it used. It declined comment on Pike's statement when contacted by the BBC.
 
This programme includes details of the process of an execution you may find upsetting.

You can watch more episodes of It Happened to Me on BBC iPlayer.

Scientists have picked up signals from the smallest scale of nature ever explored – 100 billion times smaller than an atom.
 
It's a world so small that some physicists have nicknamed it the zeptoverse.
 
The research was obtained from an experiment at the Large Hadron Collider, and could help researchers develop a new, more complete theory of how the Universe works.
 
It was led by scientists based in Cambridge, who told the BBC funding withdrawals from the UK meant the country's full involvement in the research could be in doubt.

It's polling day in the US midterm elections - millions of Americans are voting to decide who will control Congress for the final two years of Donald Trump’s presidency.
 
All 435 seats in the House; 35 of the 100 seats in the Senate; and some state-level politicians, including governors, are up for election.
 
Trump's Republican Party controls the two chambers of Congress - Democrats are hoping to flip enough seats to win a majority in both.
 
If they control Congress, Democrats would be better placed to block Trump's plans, and could also launch investigations into the president and his team.

Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel has died after he suffered a serious injury during a Spanish second-division match.
 
The 30-year-old suffered head and chest injuries during a match against FC Andorra on Monday, in a heavy collision with goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who was sent off for his challenge.
 
Spanish media, including Marca, reported De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest in the ambulance and was resuscitated by paramedics on the way to hospital.
 
The Spanish football federation announced that Tuesday's Spanish Cup fixtures had been postponed.

description:
Dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries have been hit by a cyber-attack affecting their refrigerators and freezers.
 
Around 40 Delhaize supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.
 
Sabcobel, a Belgian company that manufactures some of the affected refrigerators, said the units' evaporators were switched to defrost mode, causing them to warm up, in what is believed to be the same method used in last month's incident that hit hundreds of French supermarkets.
 
Millions of euros worth of food had to be thrown away in October, local media reported at the time.
